title: fix: autoscaler priority routing + burst controls + utilization reporting
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: Customers on Dedicated fleets observed occasional request prioritization regressions under burst load combined with incorrect fleet utilization metrics reporting. This caused unnecessary autoscaler churn and poor tail latency for higher-priority routes. Motivation: Stabilize priority-based routing under burst token consumption and ensure utilization reporting reflects true allocation (avoids double-counting cached KV usage). This is a targeted fix focusing on three areas: 1) priority routing race: ensure requests from high-priority routes bypass transient backpressure correctly; 2) tokenbucket/burst smoothing: fix token refill accounting and smoothing window to avoid large instantaneous burst drains; 3) utilization reporting: adjust metrics pipeline to exclude ephemeral cache hits and to emit per-fleet, per-priority utilization numbers. What I changed (summary): - Autoscaler/prioritizer: added a deterministic fast-path for high-priority requests that only applies when capacity headroom > configured threshold; converted a few non-atomic route checks into a single gated comparison to avoid races. - Tokenbucket & burst controls: fixed refill math for fractional tokens, tightened smoothing window from 10s to 2s for Dedicated fleets, added configurable smoothing factor on per-fleet config. - Utilization reporting: updated metrics emitter to subtract KV cache hits (prefix cache) from consumed tokens and added a new metric dedicated_autoscaler.utilization_by_priority. - Tests & docs: unit tests for refill edgecases, integration test simulating priority traffic spikes, docs update describing new smoothing config and rollout guidance. Testing & rollout: - Unit and integration test suite added and run locally (unit: 132 tests, all passing). - Staging canary for one dedicated fleet run for 24h with synthetic priority spike; observed stable tail latencies and utilization numbers matched expected baseline. - Gradual rollout plan: canary -> 10% fleets -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback if utilization deviation > 10% or 95th latency regresses by > 15%. Notes: This change is non-breaking for config (defaults preserve previous behavior except for the smoothing window improvement). The smoothing window is exposed as fleet config and can be tuned per-customer. Also added telemetry to SLO-runbook so SRE can watch the new metric during rollout.

release_notes:
- Stabilize priority-based routing under burst loads (reduces tail latency for high-priority routes)
- Fix burst tokenbucket fractional refill and smoothing behavior to avoid autoscaler churn
- Emit new metric dedicated_autoscaler.utilization_by_priority and exclude prefix cache hits from utilization calculations
- Non-breaking config: smoothing window is configurable per-fleet (default improved)
notes_for_sre: Watch dedicated_autoscaler.utilization_by_priority and dedicated_autoscaler.tokenbucket_refill_rate during rollout; automated rollback triggers: utilization deviation > 10% OR 95th latency regression > 15%.
